subject: TorchBay: sustained latency & error spike on Dedicated pool — immediate executive bridge requested
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@torchbay.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Valdez <marco@torchbay.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Production latency + errors — Dedicated pool (TorchBay)

Sofia,

We started seeing a sustained spike in latency and errors against our reserved capacity this morning after 06:30 PDT. This is impacting our ML inference SLA and user-facing transactions. Quick summary: 

- p95 latency jumped from ~0.65s -> ~3.2s
- 5xx-like model errors (generation aborts) averaged 6.3% for the 2h window
- Effective throughput against our reserved commit is ~60% of expected (requests queued/timeouted)

We attached a short tail of error logs and a perf snapshot (perf_snapshot_0712.json, error_log_tail.txt). Our Dev and SRE teams are seeing unexplained queueing in the pool that should be dedicated to our reservation.

This is now customer-impacting. We need a remediation path + ETA, and we expect Redwood to propose an immediate fallback plan (model variant, additional headroom, or temporary burst). If this becomes a prolonged SLA issue we will need a formal exec bridge.

Please confirm receipt and when you can have an ops lead join a call.

— Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Engineering, TorchBay
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@torchbay.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Production latency + errors — Dedicated pool (TorchBay)

Elena — thank you for the quick heads-up and the attachments. I see the logs and the perf snapshot; we agree this looks like sustained headroom pressure combined with anomalous error rates.

Immediate steps from our side: 
- I am opening an incident (INC-7081) and assigning ops to investigate queue depths and kernel fail/retries.
- Marissa (who leads our dedicated capacity ops) and Grace (SRE lead) are looped in — they will coordinate diagnostics and an on-call bridge.
- We will validate model variant compatibility and prepare an immediate fallback to a lower-memory variant that is compatible with your workload if we confirm KV/cache pressure.

Can you share the Grafana link (if different from the one you sent) and the exact minute window you want us to prioritize for traces? We’ll aim to have an initial ops postmortem + mitigation plan in ~90 minutes.

Call options: 08:45, 09:15, or 09:30 PDT — please confirm a time for a 30-min incident bridge.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Lead — Strategic Customers, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: [URGENT] Production latency + errors — Dedicated pool (TorchBay)

Marissa / Vivek — rolling up the initial details from TorchBay (below). Key ops asks: 

1) Heap/CPU/gpu-util trends for the dedicated pool serving DBL-9987 between 06:00–09:00 PDT. Look for kernel preemption, OOM, or throttling events.
2) KV cache hit rates and prefix lengths for the same timeframe — if KV caches are thrashing we need to reduce active worker concurrency or switch to variant-with-smaller-kv.
3) Check for any recent scheduling changes, preemption events, or model rollout in the last 24h.

I'll start a trace capture and attach the initial perf snapshot to INC-7081. If we confirm that dedicated pool is saturated we should propose: 
- Immediate: temporary burst to adjacent spare hostpool (if allowed by policy) + switch to model-variant v2-small for latency-sensitive calls
- 1–2h: scale dedicated pool (add 2 hot workers) and enable prefix caching optimization for TorchBay routes
- Exec: request for SLA exception/credit if throughput shortfall persists >4h

I'll be on the 08:45 bridge.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@torchbay.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Production latency + errors — Dedicated pool (TorchBay)

Elena — thanks for joining the 08:45 bridge. Quick update from ops and proposed immediate mitigation: 

What we found in the first 30m: 
- Dedicated pool serving TorchBay is at sustained >92% GPU utilization with queue backpressure hitting the worker scheduler.
- Several worker processes reported repeated kernel-retry events tied to a custom attention kernel; observed increase in small-abort model errors.
- No recent model rollouts or infra changes from our side in the last 24h.

Immediate mitigations we executed (live): 
- Enabled temporary burst to a nearby hot spare pool (added 2 hot workers) — visible in perf snapshot attached.
- Re-routed latency-sensitive API route to model-variant v2-small (lower memory, slightly lower quality) — this drops p95 by ~1.1s in testing.
- Bumped prefix cache TTL for your routes to improve KV hit-rate and reduce recompute.

Ask: we need an exec bridge to discuss a formal SLA remediation and an exception to allow sustained burst for up to 6 hours while we stabilize. I attached a short draft (sla-exception-draft.docx) to show proposed crediting language and timebox.

Next steps: ops will continue tracing and post the incident summary in INC-7081. We will continue to monitor and will follow up with a 2-hour readout.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Capacity & Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rossi <elena@torchbay.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Valdez <marco@torchbay.ai>, procurement@torchbay.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Production latency + errors — Dedicated pool (TorchBay)

Marissa / Sofia — appreciate the quick mitigation steps and the temporary burst. A few data points from our end post-mitigation: 

- Baseline p95 before incident: ~0.65s; peak pre-mitigation: 3.2s; post-mitigation after variant switch: ~1.1s (improvement but still above SLA target 0.8s)
- Error rate dropped from 6.3% -> 1.8% after re-route to v2-small
- Throughput: still measured ~85% of reserved commit (improved from 60%) — we see some queueing on long tail requests

We are prepared to join an exec-level call at 15:00 PDT to discuss SLA credits and longer-term capacity add. Please confirm invite and include the remediation timeline you plan to execute in the next 6 hours.

— Elena
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary + requested actions (TorchBay incident INC-7081)

Folks — post-incident summary and ask for exec decision: 

Summary (12:00 snapshot): 
- Impact: TorchBay saw p95 latency spike to 3.2s and error rate 6.3% before mitigation; after immediate mitigations p95 ~1.1s, errors 1.8%, throughput ~85% reserved commit.
- Root-cause hypothesis: Dedicated pool hit sustained kernel-level contention on a custom attention kernel leading to retries and queueing. No customer-initiated rollout or config change detected.
- Actions taken: +2 hot workers added (temporary burst), route re-directed to v2-small, prefix cache TTL increased, trace capture and logs attached to INC-7081.

Request for exec: 
1) Approve SLA exception and credit language in the attached draft for up to a 6-hour remediation window (attachment: sla-exception-draft.docx).
2) Approve short-term capacity expansion for this reserved pool (+4 workers) for 72 hours while we run an in-depth kernel / workload regression and deploy a micro-patch to the attention kernel. Estimated incremental cost: $12k/day.
3) Authorize a customer executive bridge at 15:00 PDT today — Elena confirmed availability.

If approved, we will: a) schedule the bridge and invite TorchBay execs, b) trigger capacity expansion, c) put a priority ticket with infra to fast-track kernel patch.

Please reply all with APPROVE / REJECT / NEEDS MORE INFO. We need a decision by 14:15 PDT to meet the 15:00 bridge ask.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Production Engineering, Redwood Inference
